title: SDK Seed: minimal full-stack examples (Next.js App Router, FastAPI ASGI, Go HTTP, cross-language CLIs)
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Create a small, opinionated repository of minimal starter projects demonstrating idiomatic usage patterns for Redwood SDKs across TypeScript (Next.js App Router), Python (FastAPI ASGI), Go (net/http server), and language-agnostic CLI examples. Focus areas: streaming ergonomics, retry/backoff patterns, lightweight batching, and copy-paste ready snippets that product teams can fork and iterate on.

Goals:
- Provide 4 minimal starter apps (Next.js, FastAPI, Go, CLI) that show production-minded defaults but remain tiny (under ~200 LOC per example).
- Demonstrate streaming integration end-to-end: request -> server -> client streaming consumption with reconnect and graceful cancellation.
- Show robust retry patterns with idempotency guidance, jittered exponential backoff, and when not to retry (safety rules).
- Include cookbook snippets for batching, KV prefix caching usage hints, and prompt-evaluation hooks.
- Include unit and integration tests and CI workflow templates to validate streaming and retry behavior.

Non-goals:
- Not a comprehensive SDK rework. This is examples + docs only (no API surface churn).
- Not intended to cover every framework; pick representative idioms.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Keep examples minimal: prefer clear primitives over framework magic so engineers see how the SDK is used in practice.
- Streaming ergonomics: show both pull-based (async iterator in Python/TS) and push-based (ReadableStream in browser Next.js) consumption. Include an example of backpressure handling in the browser using TransformStream.
- Retries: include a small retry library wrapper used in examples (algs: full jitter exponential backoff). Surface clearly where user must provide idempotency keys (non-idempotent write flows).
- Telemetry: examples will include a small metrics stub (latency tokens, retry count) and instrumentation notes for Console integration.

Example highlights (what each starter contains):
- Next.js App Router (TS): server route that proxies streaming generation responses and performs server-side rendering progressive hydration. Demonstrates fetch + ReadableStream + Response(stream) with reconnection token and progress indicator. Uses the SDK's streaming callback pattern and a tiny client helper (useStreaming() hook) that returns an async iterator for UI consumption.
- FastAPI ASGI (Python): async endpoint that yields generator chunks from the SDK streaming client. Demonstrates request cancellation via request.state and background task to flush metrics. Includes example of using retry wrapper for idempotent submit endpoints.
- Go net/http server: minimal HTTP handler that streams tokens with http.Flusher and context cancellation. Shows middleware that injects realistic retry headers (Idempotency-Key) and demonstrates a small batching helper for embedding calls.
- Cross-language CLIs: two tiny CLIs (Typer-based Python and Cobra-based Go) showing both streaming to stdout and file-based checkpointing for long-running jobs. CLI shows interruption handling and resume by saving last token offsets.

Cookbook snippets included in repo:
- Batching patterns for chat/embedding use-cases with heuristics (max tokens, max items, flush interval).
- KV prefix cache example for conversational contexts.
- Prompt templating best practices: safe placeholders, structured output checks.
- Retry policy snippets: when to retry, idempotency for calls that append vs update, example list of retryable status codes and quota handling.

Acceptance criteria:
- Repository lives at github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples with branch ENG-22478 seeded.
- Each starter has README.md with copy-paste instructions, minimal Dockerfile (for FastAPI/Go), and a single test that validates streaming works end-to-end in CI.
- A short guide (one-page) explaining recommended retry defaults and idempotency guidance for internal docs/Console linking.
- PR reviewed by at least one SDK eng (Ravi) and one DevRel/design reviewer.

Next steps / tasks:
1) Create monorepo scaffold and README that maps to quickstarts (owner: Ravi).
2) Implement Next.js example focusing on ReadableStream and numeric progress UX (owner: SOC intern + Ravi).
3) Implement FastAPI generator endpoint and background flush (owner: Priya Rao).
4) Implement minimal Go server and CLI sample (owner: Tomasz Nowak).
5) Add CI workflow that runs the streaming integration test in headless mode and fails on regressions (owner: DevRel).

Risks and mitigations:
- Complexity in streaming reconnection: mitigate by providing simple helper utilities and a documented reconnect token strategy.
- Misuse of retries causing duplicate side effects: mitigate by documenting idempotency patterns and instrumenting examples with explicit idempotency-key usage.

Dependencies and notes:
- Reuses patterns from ENG-20891 (sample templates) but intentionally smaller and more focused on runtime behaviors.
- Align with Console telemetry hooks to expose per-route token counts in examples.

Deliverables:
- GitHub repo with 4 example folders: nextjs-app, fastapi-app, go-server, cli-examples.
- CI/Integration test job and short HOWTO on using examples as templates for customer onboarding.

Estimated effort: ~8 story points across 2 sprints.

- Design notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/SDK/ENG-22478+seed+examples
- Related tickets: ENG-20891 (sample apps), ENG-15234 (consolidated examples)
